issues.body: `_agent_from_role_flag` validates only that the value is a boolean, then returns it. Consequently, a match-label route containing `agent_from_role = false` is accepted and behaves exactly as if the declaration were absent. The new README contract says that anything but boolean `true` fails closed, and the implementation comments describe the option as an explicit declaration; accepting `false` creates the same inert-declaration hazard that the code correctly rejects on role/default tables. The PLAN resolver mirrors this acceptance, so cross-resolver agreement remains green and cannot detect a maintainer typo or an incorrectly generated value. The self-tests cover strings, integers, lists, and null, but omit the only value-identical survivor: `False`.
issues.fix_hint: When the key is present on an allowed match-label route, require its value to be exactly `True`; reject explicit `False` in both `policy-resolve.py` and `route-resolve.py`. Add red tests for `agent_from_role = false` to both resolver self-tests and the cross-resolver malformed-declaration checks. If explicit false is intentionally supported, revise all fail-closed documentation and add a non-vacuous test that pins that alternative contract.
issues.title: Explicit `agent_from_role = false` is silently accepted instead of failing closed

verdict.summary: The role-directed persona design is implemented consistently across PLAN and CLAIM for `true`, and the worker seam is guarded by the declared fix capability. However, the new declaration is not fail-closed according to its own documented contract: an explicit boolean `false` is accepted as a silent no-op even though the README and code comments say anything other than boolean `true` must be rejected. Because this is trust-plane configuration and both resolvers currently agree on accepting the inert value, the agreement gate will not expose the mistake.
